name: Overhead Rope Cable Triceps Extension
nameDa: Overhead tricepsextension med reb i kabel
grip: One rope end in each hand, palms facing each other and wrists aligned with the forearms.
description: Extend both elbows with the upper arms overhead while a rope connects to a cable behind the body.
setup: Attach the rope to a low pulley and select a manageable stack setting.
Bring the rope behind the head and step into a stable staggered stance facing away from the stack.
Raise the upper arms beside the head and establish cable tension without arching the back.
instructions: Begin with elbows bent and hands behind the head in a comfortable position.
Straighten the elbows while keeping the upper arms nearly stationary.
Finish overhead without forcing the elbows into hyperextension.
Bend the elbows slowly to return; keep the cable controlled when ending the set.
cues: Let the rope ends move naturally.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to raise the hands.
Swinging the shoulders or letting the stack pull the arms back suddenly.

logging.example: A single stack selected at 20 kg: record 20 kg on that machine.
logging.note: Record the selected stack value, attachment and pulley setup. Pulley ratios and machine calibration make stack values unsuitable for direct comparisons across machines.

variantNote: Overhead rope version, distinct from a pushdown. A low pulley behind the standing athlete is the illustrated assumption; a high-pulley forward-leaning version needs its own setup.
reviewNotes: Overhead rope attachment is confirmed; exact pulley height and stance still need equipment review.
The source's seated low-pulley setup supports the rope and elbow action, not validation of the illustrated standing adaptation.
